title: When he first felt discrimination in Cuba
summary: His father's wealth shielded him until he started working with Maria Teresa at the Academia El Encanto, where musicians were kept from mixing with the clientele.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Uh Huh - Macho, when did you first become aware of discrimination in Cuba? About how old were you?

Well, when I was seventeen. I never had, never feel the pressure because I - we don't have - I don't have to work to live. I went to school with the Prio Socarras brothers, the small ones. We went to a private school. I had no problems. My economy liberate me. Like it always happen in every country; when you had economy you don't feel as much pressure.
In other words, your father's business made you one of the fortunate Afro-Cubans uh? - - -
- - - - who were better off than the average ones. But when were you - tell me about this time that you became aware of the discrimination against Afro-Cubans.

Well, when I start working. Well, I heard about it, but I never, I never went through the - the - I mean physically or spiritually, whatever; so when I start really making living for myself, because I quit school, and I don't want to ask my father anything, I want to make my own living, so I went to work with Maria Teresa, We used to work at the Academia El Encanto and they - there was a restriction.
We just couldn't talk with nobody, especially with the women, they were white; and a certain restriction that make you aware that their world was different that the one that I used to live.
In other words, You had a different door that you had to come in through? And you had to leave that way too?
What about fountains of water? Did they have one for whites and one for blacks?

No, no, no, no it just was that we - they didn't want us to be mixing with the - with the costumer and with the people they consider that we don't supposed to because I, I don't know, it was so silly.
Was this for the white Cuban also? He couldn't mix with the costumer?
Yes. Those - they had more privileges that what we had, but still, there was kind of restriction for them too because the costumer they were jealous about
you know, the women like the musicians. They like to talk to them, ask for numbers and this and that, and there was in a way, more to prefer the working class not be mixed......
Mixing with the elite or society.
